segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
38 the captives of the Jews who were in Egypt,
and he sent offerings to Eleazar the high priest, and requested the Holy Scriptures and translators.
He, then, wrote the Scriptures in gold,
and sent them with seventy-two wise men who were proficient in both languages, Greek and Hebrew,
six from each tribe.
And the king settled them on the island of Pharos (Pharos?);
and he built for them thirty-six cells,
one for every two,
while warning them that they should not alter anything.
And they translated the Scriptures in seventy-two days,
each pair translating all of them.
They were thirty-six translations,
and when they were compared with one another,
they were found to agree,
as though one person had translated them.
And the king placed them in his library in Alexandria.
And in his twenty-fourth year, Antiochus, who was called God (Theos), reigned over Syria after Antiochus Soter for fifteen years.
And in his thirty-fourth year, the Parthians, that is, the Persians {OCR?}, rebelled against the Macedonians, that is, the Greeks,
and they set up for themselves a king named Arsaces,
and from then on they were called Arsacids.
And at this time the Romans killed up to forty thousand of the Gauls and Celts (Galatians?).
And Rhodes and all the regions around it were shaken,
so that even the great Colossus fell.
And they also pressed Syracuse hard in war,
and they also destroyed Capua.
And Sicily was subjugated to them,
and likewise many cities in Iberia (Spain?).
After Philadelphus, Ptolemy Euergetes, that is,
the Benefactor,
twenty-six years.
And in this same year, Seleucus Callinicus reigned in Syria for twenty years.
And he built Callinicus, which is Raqqa,
and Circesium.
And after him, Seleucus Ceraunus, three years.
And after him, Antiochus the Great, thirty-six years.
Now Onias the high priest, when he was not willing to give the customary tribute to the king of Egypt,
the king became enraged and prepared to destroy the Jews.
Then Joseph, a shrewd and energetic man, was sent to him by the Jews,
and he became his friend,
and appeased his anger, and also received authority from Euergetes.
